name: Reading First's improvements in teaching justify judging the program successful.
description: This position treats better classroom instruction as a sufficient benefit despite unproven comprehension gains. Whether that warrants a success judgment is an evaluative question, not a conclusion established by the report.
opponentName: Reading First should not be judged successful without demonstrated gains in reading comprehension.

rationale.support: The observed increases in instructional time and explicit instruction establish the teaching benefits invoked by the evaluative parent. They inform but do not establish its success criterion; the three contrasts share one evaluation.
rationale.opposition: The existing parent requires demonstrated comprehension gains for success, whereas this parent accepts improved instruction as sufficient. Link the two evaluative criteria as opposing arguments in both directions.
rationale.context: Nonsignificant print-engagement estimates qualify the breadth of implementation benefits but do not directly refute the chosen success criterion; keep Related-only links.
rationale.relatedParent: The decoding-based success judgment is a distinct alternative rationale, not a duplicate of an instruction-based judgment or automatic evidence for it.

discoveryDecision: The complete 95-entity Reading First name search found two existing success-criterion Claims, neither asserting instruction improvements as sufficient; reuse both as neighbors and create this distinct evaluative proposition.
